title: Chemical calculations - 123 school
heading: Chemical calculations
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: Which three particles do you find in an atom? Also give their abbreviations
questions.a: Protons, neutrons and electrons; p, n, e<sup>-</sup>

questions.q: Which particles give the atom most of its mass?
questions.a: Protons and neutrons

questions.q: In which unit is the mass of atoms expressed?
questions.a: atomic mass units (u)

questions.q: What determines the atomic number?
questions.a: The number of protons in the nucleus

questions.q: What does the mass number show?
questions.a: mass number = the number of protons + the number of neutrons

questions.q: What is the overview of all atoms called?
questions.a: The periodic table

questions.q: What is the ratio between protons and electrons? Explain why.
questions.a: Protons have an elementary charge of 1+, electrons of -1. In the atomic model atoms are neutral. So there are as many electrons as protons.

questions.q: Name two atomic models and one difference between them.
questions.a: The Rutherford model, in which electrons move around a nucleus in 1 cloud, and the Bohr model, in which electrons move around the nucleus in shells.

questions.q: Where are the 3 atomic particles located?
questions.a: p and n in the nucleus, electrons in different shells relatively far from the nucleus

questions.q: What are the outermost electrons called?
questions.a: Valence electrons

questions.q: Name 3 electron shells, their position relative to each other and how many electrons they can hold
questions.a: Seen from the nucleus the first three shells are K, L, M; with 2, 8 and 18 electrons respectively.

questions.q: What is meant by noble gas configuration?
questions.a: The electron configuration in which the shells are exactly filled to the maximum.

questions.q: How many valence electrons does magnesium have? (use BINAS table 99)
questions.a: Magnesium has atomic number 12 (BINAS table 99), with configuration K = 2, L = 8 and M = 2, so there are 2 electrons in the outer shell, so 2 valence electrons.

questions.q: What does magnesium need to reach the noble gas configuration?
questions.a: Lose two electrons from the M shell; Mg<sup>2+</sup> is formed

questions.q: What is the molecular mass of sulfuric acid, H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>? (use BINAS table 99)
In which group are the halogens?
questions.a: in group 17

questions.q: In which group are the noble gases?
questions.a: in group 18

questions.q: Elements in a group have similar …
questions.a: chemical properties

questions.q: How can sodium reach a noble gas configuration?
questions.a: By losing its one valence electron; Na<sup>+</sup> is formed.

questions.q: How can fluorine (F) reach a noble gas configuration?
questions.a: F has atomic number 9: with K: 2 and L: 7 electrons. By gaining an electron F gets the noble gas configuration and F<sup>-</sup> is formed

questions.q: Explain what isotopes are.
questions.a: Isotopes are atoms with the same atomic number but a different mass number. They have the same number of protons and a different number of neutrons.

questions.q: The mass number in the periodic table is almost never a round number. Explain what isotopes have to do with this.
questions.a: The mass number in the periodic table is the weighted average of the different isotopes that occur in nature.

questions.q: The relative atomic mass of chlorine is 35.45 u and the natural isotopes are Cl-35 and Cl-37. Explain which isotope is the most abundant in nature.
questions.a: 35.45 u is closer to 35 u than to 37 u. So Cl-35 will occur more often than Cl-37. Check: BINAS table 25A: 75.78% is Cl-35 and 24.22% is Cl-37.

questions.q: BINAS table 25A: which isotopes of bromine occur in nature?
questions.a: Br-79 and Br-81

questions.q: Give the atomic composition of both isotopes of bromine.
questions.a: Br-79: Br has atomic number 35, so 35 protons. The number of neutrons is 79 − 35 = 44. There are 35 electrons arranged over four shells: 2, 8, 18, 7. Br-81: also has 35 protons, but (81 − 35 =) 46 neutrons, and also 35 electrons arranged over four shells: 2, 8, 18, 7.

questions.q: How many hydrogen atoms are there in 3.5 mol of water?
questions.a: 1 mol of water contains 2 mol of H atoms, so 3.5 mol of water contains 2 × 3.5 = 7.0 mol of H atoms

questions.q: C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub> (g) and oxygen gas react to form carbon dioxide and water. Write the reaction equation using the step-by-step method.
questions.a: Step 1 (reaction scheme in words): ethane (g) + oxygen (g) -> carbon dioxide (g) + water (l). Step 2 (reaction scheme in molecular formulae): C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub> (g) + O<sub>2</sub> (g) -> CO<sub>2</sub> (g) + H<sub>2</sub>O (l). Step 3 (atom balance - balancing): C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub> (g) + 3½O<sub>2</sub> (g) -> 2CO<sub>2</sub> (g) + 3H<sub>2</sub>O (l). Step 4 (simplifying the reaction equation): 2C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub> (g) + 7O<sub>2</sub> (g) -> 4CO<sub>2</sub> (g) + 6H<sub>2</sub>O (l).

questions.q: In which mole ratio does ethane burn in the reaction above?
In a reactor you let 2 mol of ethane react with 14 mol of oxygen. Is there an excess or a shortage of oxygen?
questions.a: Excess (2× as much as needed)

questions.q: Give the scientific notation of 0.0023 mol
questions.a: 2.3 ∙ 10<sup>-3</sup> mol
